leaves.heading: § 40.1 Who does this regulation cover?
leaves.text: This part tells all parties who conduct drug and alcohol tests required by Department of Transportation (DOT) agency regulations how to conduct these tests and what procedures to use.

leaves.heading: § 40.1 Who does this regulation cover?
leaves.text: This part concerns the activities of transportation employers, safety-sensitive transportation employees (including self-employed individuals, contractors and volunteers as covered by DOT agency regulations), and service agents.

leaves.heading: § 40.1 Who does this regulation cover?
leaves.text: Nothing in this part is intended to supersede or conflict with the implementation of the Federal Railroad Administration's post-accident testing program (see 49 CFR 219.200).

leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?
leaves.text: In this part, the terms listed in this section have the following meanings:

A specimen that has been altered, as evidenced by test results showing either a substance that is not a normal constituent for that type of specimen or showing an abnormal concentration of an endogenous substance.
leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?

leaves.text: Persons are affiliates of one another if, directly or indirectly, one controls or has the power to control the other, or a third party controls or has the power to control both. Indicators of control include, but are not limited to: interlocking management or ownership; shared interest among family members; shared facilities or equipment; or common use of employees. Following the issuance of a public interest exclusion, an organization having the same or similar management, ownership, or principal employees as the service agent concerning whom a public interest exclusion is in effect is regarded as an affiliate. This definition is used in connection with the public interest exclusion procedures of Subpart R of this part.
leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?

leaves.text: In evidential breath testing devices (EBTs) using gas chromatography technology, a reading of the device's internal standard. In all other EBTs, a reading of ambient air containing no alcohol.

leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?

leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?

leaves.heading: § 40.3 What do the terms used in this part mean?

leaves.text: An authorized specimen, other than the type of specimen previously collected or attempted to be collected.

leaves.text: This number serves as a unique identifier that must be used on the Federal Drug Testing Custody and Control Form (CCF) or Alcohol Testing Form (ATF) for a donor, on the MRO's reports, on SAP reports, or on other documents that are required under this part. § 40.5 Who issues authoritative interpretations of this regulation?
leaves.text: ODAPC and the DOT Office of General Counsel (OGC) provide written interpretations of the provisions of this part. These written DOT interpretations are the only official and authoritative interpretations concerning the provisions of this part. DOT agencies may incorporate ODAPC/OGC interpretations in written guidance they issue concerning drug and alcohol testing matters. Only Part 40 interpretations issued after August 1, 2001, are considered valid.

leaves.heading: § 40.7 How can you get an exemption from a requirement in this regulation?
leaves.text: If you want an exemption from any provision of this part, you must request it in writing from the Office of the Secretary of Transportation, under the provisions and standards of 49 CFR part 5. You must send requests for an exemption to the following address: Department of Transportation, Deputy Assistant General Counsel for Regulation and Enforcement, 1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE., Washington, DC 20590.

leaves.heading: § 40.7 How can you get an exemption from a requirement in this regulation?
leaves.text: Under the standards of 49 CFR part 5, we will grant the request only if the request documents special or exceptional circumstances, not likely to be generally applicable and not contemplated in connection with the rulemaking that established this part, that make your compliance with a specific provision of this part impracticable.

leaves.heading: § 40.7 How can you get an exemption from a requirement in this regulation?
leaves.text: If we grant you an exemption, you must agree to take steps we specify to comply with the intent of the provision from which an exemption is granted.

leaves.heading: § 40.7 How can you get an exemption from a requirement in this regulation?
leaves.text: We will issue written responses to all exemption requests.

leaves.heading: § 40.11 What are the general responsibilities of employers under this regulation?
leaves.text: As an employer, you are responsible for meeting all applicable requirements and procedures of this part.

leaves.heading: § 40.11 What are the general responsibilities of employers under this regulation?
leaves.text: You are responsible for all actions of your officials, representatives, and agents (including service agents) in carrying out the requirements of the DOT agency regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.11 What are the general responsibilities of employers under this regulation?
leaves.text: All agreements and arrangements, written or unwritten, between and among employers and service agents concerning the implementation of DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements are deemed, as a matter of law, to require compliance with all applicable provisions of this part and DOT agency drug and alcohol testing regulations. Compliance with these provisions is a material term of all such agreements and arrangements.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: DOT tests must be completely separate from non-DOT tests in all respects.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: DOT tests must take priority and must be conducted and completed before a non-DOT test is begun. When conducting a urine DOT drug test, you must discard any excess urine left over from a DOT test and collect a separate urine void for the subsequent non-DOT test.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, you must not perform any tests on DOT specimens other than those tests specifically authorized by this part or DOT agency regulations. For example, you must not test a DOT specimen for additional drugs. In addition, a laboratory is prohibited from making a DOT specimen available for a DNA test or other types of specimen identity testing.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: When a DOT urine drug test collection is conducted as part of a physical examination required by DOT agency regulations, it is permissible to conduct medical tests related to this physical examination ( e.g., for glucose) on any specimen remaining in the collection container after the DOT portion has been sealed into the specimen bottles.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: A non-DOT drug or alcohol test administered, as part of a physical examination, is not a DOT drug or alcohol test for purposes of this part and/or related DOT agency drug and alcohol testing rules, if that test was performed to determine if an employee is medically qualified for a license or certificate. Consequently, the results of such a test do not have consequences under this part.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: No one is permitted to change or disregard the results of DOT tests based on the results of non-DOT tests. For example, as an employer you must not disregard a verified positive DOT drug test result because the employee presents a negative test result from a blood or urine specimen collected by the employee's physician or a DNA test result purporting to question the identity of the DOT specimen.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must not use the CCF or the ATF in your non-DOT drug and alcohol testing programs. This prohibition includes the use of the DOT forms with references to DOT programs and agencies crossed out. You also must always use the CCF and ATF for all your DOT-mandated drug and alcohol tests.

leaves.heading: § 40.13 How do DOT drug and alcohol tests relate to non-DOT tests?
leaves.text: No one is permitted to conduct a DOT drug or alcohol test on an individual who is not a DOT-regulated employee, as defined by the DOT agency regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: As an employer, or an employer's service agent—for example a C/TPA, you must ensure the collector has the following information when conducting a specimen collection for you:

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Full name of the employee being tested.

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: SSN or Employee ID No.

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Laboratory name and address (can be pre-printed on the CCF).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Employer name, address, phone number, and fax number (can be pre-printed on the CCF at Step 1-A).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: DER information required at § 40.36.

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: MRO name, address, phone number, and fax number (can be pre-printed on the CCF at Step 1-B).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: The DOT Agency which regulates the employee's safety-sensitive duties (the checkmark can pre-printed in the appropriate box on the CCF at Step 1-D).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Test reason, as appropriate: Pre-employment; Random; Reasonable Suspicion/Reasonable Cause; Post-Accident; Return-to-Duty; and Follow-up.

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Whether the test is to be observed or not (see § 40.67 of this part).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: (Optional) C/TPA name, address, phone, and fax number (can be pre-printed on the CCF).

leaves.heading: § 40.14 What collection information must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: Specimen type to be collected ( i.e., oral fluid or urine).

leaves.heading: § 40.15 May an employer use a service agent to meet DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements?
leaves.text: As an employer, you may use a service agent to perform the tasks needed to comply with this part and DOT agency drug and alcohol testing regulations, consistent with the requirements of Subpart Q and other applicable provisions of this part.

leaves.heading: § 40.15 May an employer use a service agent to meet DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements?
leaves.text: As an employer, you are responsible for ensuring that the service agents you use meet the qualifications set forth in this part ( e.g., § 40.121 for MROs). You may require service agents to show you documentation that they meet the requirements of this part ( e.g., documentation of MRO qualifications required by § 40.121(e)).

leaves.heading: § 40.15 May an employer use a service agent to meet DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements?
leaves.text: You remain responsible for compliance with all applicable requirements of this part and other DOT drug and alcohol testing regulations, even when you use a service agent. If you violate this part or other DOT drug and alcohol testing regulations because a service agent has not provided services as our rules require, a DOT agency can subject you to sanctions. Your good faith use of a service agent is not a defense in an enforcement action initiated by a DOT agency in which your alleged noncompliance with this part or a DOT agency drug and alcohol regulation may have resulted from the service agent's conduct.

leaves.heading: § 40.15 May an employer use a service agent to meet DOT drug and alcohol testing requirements?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must not permit a service agent to act as your DER.

leaves.heading: § 40.17 Is an employer responsible for obtaining information from its service agents?
leaves.text: Yes, as an employer, you are responsible for obtaining information required by this part from your service agents. This is true whether or not you choose to use a C/TPA as an intermediary in transmitting information to you. For example, suppose an applicant for a safety-sensitive job takes a pre-employment drug test, but there is a significant delay in your receipt of the test result from an MRO or C/TPA. You must not assume that “no news is good news” and permit the applicant to perform safety-sensitive duties before receiving the result. This is a violation of the Department's regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.21 May an employer stand down an employee before the MRO has completed the verification process?
leaves.text: As an employer, you are prohibited from standing employees down, except consistent with a waiver a DOT agency grants under this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.21 May an employer stand down an employee before the MRO has completed the verification process?
leaves.text: You may make a request to the concerned DOT agency for a waiver from the prohibition of paragraph (a) of this section. Such a waiver, if granted, permits you to stand an employee down following the MRO's receipt of a laboratory report of a confirmed positive test for a drug or drug metabolite, an adulterated test, or a substituted test pertaining to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.21 May an employer stand down an employee before the MRO has completed the verification process?
leaves.text: For this purpose, the concerned DOT agency is the one whose drug and alcohol testing rules apply to the majority of the covered employees in your organization. The concerned DOT agency uses its applicable procedures for considering requests for waivers.

context.text: You may make a request to the concerned DOT agency for a waiver from the prohibition of paragraph (a) of this section. Such a waiver, if granted, permits you to stand an employee down following the MRO's receipt of a laboratory report of a confirmed positive test for a drug or drug metabolite, an adulterated test, or a substituted test pertaining to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.21 May an employer stand down an employee before the MRO has completed the verification process?
leaves.text: Before taking action on a waiver request, the concerned DOT agency coordinates with other DOT agencies that regulate the employer's other covered employees.

leaves.heading: § 40.21 May an employer stand down an employee before the MRO has completed the verification process?
leaves.text: You must not stand employees down in the absence of a waiver, or inconsistent with the terms of your waiver. If you do, you are in violation of this part and DOT agency drug testing regulations, and you are subject to enforcement action by the DOT agency just as you are for other violations of this part and DOT agency rules.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives a verified positive drug test result, you must immediately remove the employee involved from performing safety-sensitive functions. You must take this action upon receiving the initial report of the verified positive test result. Do not wait to receive the written report or the result of a split specimen test.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives a verified adulterated or substituted drug test result, you must consider this a refusal to test and immediately remove the employee involved from performing safety-sensitive functions. You must take this action on receiving the initial report of the verified adulterated or substituted test result. Do not wait to receive the written report or the result of a split specimen test.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives an alcohol test result of 0.04 or higher, you must immediately remove the employee involved from performing safety-sensitive functions. If you receive an alcohol test result of 0.02-0.039, you must temporarily remove the employee involved from performing safety-sensitive functions, as provided in applicable DOT agency regulations. Do not wait to receive the written report of the result of the test.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer, when an employee has a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted test result, or has otherwise violated a DOT agency drug and alcohol regulation, you must not return the employee to the performance of safety-sensitive functions until or unless the employee successfully completes the return-to-duty process of Subpart O of this part.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's specimen was dilute, take action as provided in § 40.197.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: You must immediately direct the employee to provide a new specimen under direct observation (either an oral fluid specimen or a urine specimen under direct observation).

context.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: You must not attach consequences to the finding that the test was invalid other than collecting a new specimen under direct observation.

context.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: You must not give any advance notice of this test requirement to the employee.

context.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: You must instruct the collector to note on the CCF the same reason ( e.g., random test, post-accident test) and DOT Agency (e.g., check DOT and FMCSA) as for the original collection.

context.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: You must ensure that the collector conducts the collection under direct observation (either an oral fluid specimen or a urine specimen under direct observation).

context.text: As an employer who receives a drug test result indicating that the employee's test was cancelled because it was invalid and that a second collection must take place under direct observation—

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer who receives a cancelled test result when a negative result is required ( e.g., pre-employment, return-to-duty, or follow-up test), you must direct the employee to provide another specimen immediately.

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer, you may also be required to take additional actions required by DOT agency regulations ( e.g., FAA rules require some positive drug tests to be reported to the Federal Air Surgeon).

leaves.heading: § 40.23 What actions do employers take after receiving verified test results?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must not alter a drug or alcohol test result transmitted to you by an MRO, BAT, or C/TPA.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: Yes, as an employer, you must, after obtaining an employee's written consent, request the information about the employee listed in paragraphs (b) through (j) of this section. This requirement applies only to employees seeking to begin performing safety-sensitive duties for you for the first time ( i.e., a new hire, an employee transferring into a safety-sensitive position). If the employee refuses to provide this written consent, you must not permit the employee to perform safety-sensitive functions.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: If you are an employer regulated by FMCSA, you must comply with the requirements of this section by using the FMCSA's Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse in accordance with 49 CFR 382.71(a). In addition, you must continue to comply with the requirements of this § 40.25 when checking an employee's testing history with employers regulated by a DOT operating administration other than FMCSA.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: If you are an employer regulated by FMCSA, with a prospective employee subject to drug and alcohol testing with a DOT agency other than FMCSA, you must continue to request the information about the employee listed in paragraphs (b) through (j) of this section. For example, if you are an employer regulated by both FMCSA and PHMSA, and you are hiring an employee to perform functions regulated by both DOT agencies, then you must query FMCSA's Clearinghouse to satisfy FMCSA's requirements and you must request the information listed in paragraphs (b) through (j) of this section to satisfy PHMSA's requirements.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: Alcohol tests with a result of 0.04 or higher alcohol concentration;

context.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: Verified positive drug tests;

context.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: Refusals to be tested (including verified adulterated or substituted drug test results);

context.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: Other violations of DOT agency drug and alcohol testing regulations; and

context.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: With respect to any employee who violated a DOT drug and alcohol regulation, documentation of the employee's successful completion of DOT return-to-duty requirements (including follow-up tests). If the previous employer does not have information about the return-do-duty process ( e.g., an employer who did not hire an employee who tested positive on a pre-employment test), you must seek to obtain this information from the employee.

context.text: You must request the information listed in this paragraph (b) from DOT-regulated employers who have employed the employee during any period during the two years before the date of the employee's application or transfer:

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: The information obtained from a previous employer includes any drug or alcohol test information obtained from previous employers under this section or other applicable DOT agency regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: If feasible, you must obtain and review this information before the employee first performs safety-sensitive functions. If this is not feasible, you must obtain and review the information as soon as possible. However, you must not permit the employee to perform safety-sensitive functions after 30 days from the date on which the employee first performed safety-sensitive functions, unless you have obtained or made and documented a good faith effort to obtain this information.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: If you obtain information that the employee has violated a DOT agency drug and alcohol regulation, you must not use the employee to perform safety-sensitive functions unless you also obtain information that the employee has subsequently complied with the return-to-duty requirements of Subpart O of this part and DOT agency drug and alcohol regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: You must provide to each of the employers from whom you request information under paragraph (b) of this section written consent for the release of the information cited in paragraph (a) of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: The release of information under this section must be in any written form ( e.g., fax, e-mail, letter) that ensures confidentiality. As the previous employer, you must maintain a written record of the information released, including the date, the party to whom it was released, and a summary of the information provided.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: If you are an employer from whom information is requested under paragraph (b) of this section, you must, after reviewing the employee's specific, written consent, immediately release the requested information to the employer making the inquiry.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: As the employer requesting the information required under this section, you must maintain a written, confidential record of the information you obtain or of the good faith efforts you made to obtain the information. You must retain this information for three years from the date of the employee's first performance of safety-sensitive duties for you.

leaves.heading: § 40.25 Must an employer check on the drug and alcohol testing record of employees it is intending to use to perform safety-sensitive duties?
leaves.text: As the employer, you must also ask the employee whether he or she has tested positive, or refused to test, on any pre-employment drug or alcohol test administered by an employer to which the employee applied for, but did not obtain, safety-sensitive transportation work covered by DOT agency drug and alcohol testing rules during the past two years. If the employee admits that he or she had a positive test or a refusal to test, you must not use the employee to perform safety-sensitive functions for you, until and unless the employee documents successful completion of the return-to-duty process (see paragraphs (b)(5) and (e) of this section).

leaves.heading: § 40.26 What form must an employer use to report Management Information System (MIS) data to a DOT agency?
leaves.text: As an employer, when you are required to report MIS data to a DOT agency, you must use the U.S. Department of Transportation Drug and Alcohol Testing MIS Data Collection Form to report that data. You must use the form and instructions referenced at appendix J to part 40. You must submit the MIS report in accordance with rule requirements ( e.g., dates for submission; selection of companies required to submit, and method of reporting) established by the DOT agency regulating your operation.

leaves.heading: § 40.27 May an employer require an employee to sign a consent or release in connection with the DOT drug and alcohol testing program?
leaves.text: No, as an employer, you must not require an employee to sign a consent, release, waiver of liability, or indemnification agreement with respect to any part of the drug or alcohol testing process covered by this part (including, but not limited to, collections, laboratory testing, MRO and SAP services).

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: Collectors meeting the requirements of this subpart are the only persons authorized to collect urine specimens for DOT drug testing.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: A urine collector must meet training requirements of § 40.33.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: An oral fluid collector must meet the training requirements of § 40.35.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: To avoid the appearance of a conflict of interest, if you are the immediate supervisor of the employee being tested, you must not act as the collector when that employee is tested, unless no other collector is available and you are permitted to do so under DOT agency drug and alcohol regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: You must not act as the collector for the employee being tested if you work for a HHS-certified laboratory ( e.g., as a technician or accessioner) and could link the employee with a urine specimen, drug testing result, or laboratory report.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: Employees are not permitted to be their own collector.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: An employee who is a qualified collector is not permitted to be their own collector; another qualified collector must perform the collection in accordance with this part.

context.text: Employees are not permitted to be their own collector.

leaves.heading: § 40.31 Who may collect specimens for DOT drug testing?
leaves.text: To avoid a potential conflict of interest, a collector must not be related to the employee being tested ( e.g., spouse, ex-spouse, relative) or a close personal friend.

context.text: Employees are not permitted to be their own collector.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: To be permitted to act as a urine collector in the DOT drug testing program, you must meet each of the requirements of this section:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: You must be knowledgeable about this part, the current “DOT Urine Specimen Collection Procedures Guidelines,” and DOT agency regulations applicable to the employers for whom you perform collections. DOT agency regulations, the DOT Urine Specimen Collection Procedures Guidelines, and other materials are available from ODAPC (Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE., Washington DC, 20590, 202-366-3784, or on the ODAPC Web site ( https://www.transportation.gov/odapc ). You must keep current on any changes to these materials. You must subscribe to the ODAPC list-serve at: https://www.transportation.gov/odapc/get-odapc-email-updates.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph. Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: All steps necessary to complete a collection correctly and the proper completion and transmission of the CCF;

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph. Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: “Problem” collections ( e.g., situations like “shy bladder” and attempts to tamper with a specimen);

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph. Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Fatal flaws, correctable flaws, and how to correct problems in collections; and

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph. Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: The collector's responsibility for maintaining the integrity of the collection process, ensuring the privacy of employees being tested, ensuring the security of the specimen, and avoiding conduct or statements that could be viewed as offensive or inappropriate;

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph. Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: The five mock collections must include two uneventful collection scenarios, one insufficient quantity of urine scenario, one temperature out of range scenario, and one scenario in which the employee refuses to sign the CCF and initial the specimen bottle tamper-evident seal.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between the instructor and trainee, and attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” This person must be a qualified urine collector who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by—

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Regularly conducting DOT urine drug test collections for a period of at least one year;

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between the instructor and trainee, and attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” This person must be a qualified urine collector who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by—

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Conducting urine collector training under this part for at least one year; or

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between the instructor and trainee, and attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” This person must be a qualified urine collector who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by—

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Successfully completing a urine “train the trainer” course.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections.

Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between the instructor and trainee, and attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” This person must be a qualified urine collector who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by—

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: You must meet the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section before you begin to perform collector functions.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: No less frequently than every five years from the date on which you satisfactorily complete the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, you must complete refresher training that meets all the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: If you make a mistake in the collection process that causes a test to be cancelled ( i.e., a fatal or uncorrected flaw), you must undergo error correction training. This training must occur within 30 days of the date you are notified of the error that led to the need for retraining. Errors that cause cancellation but occur outside the collection process ( e.g., when a specimen is crushed or otherwise damaged during the transportation process, or is lost in transit), the cancellation would not be the result of an error by the collector during the collection process and does not require the collector to be retrained.

leaves.heading: § 40.33 What training requirements must a collector meet for urine collection?
leaves.text: Error correction training must be provided and your proficiency documented in writing by a person who meets the requirements of paragraph (c)(2) of this section.

leaves.text: As part of the error correction training, you must demonstrate your proficiency in the collection procedures of this part by completing three consecutive error-free mock collections. The person providing the training must monitor and evaluate your performance and attest in writing that the mock collections were “error-free.”

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: To be permitted to act as an oral fluid collector in the DOT drug testing program, you must meet each of the requirements of this section:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: You must be knowledgeable about this part, the current “DOT Oral Fluid Specimen Collection Procedures Guidelines,” and DOT agency regulations applicable to the employers for whom you perform collections. DOT agency regulations, guidelines, and other materials are available from ODAPC (Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington DC, 20590, 202-366-3784, or on the ODAPC website ( https://www.transportation.gov/odapc ). You must keep current on any changes to these materials. You must subscribe to the ODAPC list-serve at: https://www.transportation.gov/odapc/get-odapc-email-updates.

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: Training on the testing procedures of this part;

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.text: Training to proficiency in the operation of the particular oral fluid collection device(s) you will be using.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: All steps necessary to complete a collection correctly and the proper completion and transmission of the CCF;

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: “Problem” collections ( e.g., situations like “dry mouth” and attempts to tamper with a specimen);

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: Fatal flaws, correctable flaws, and how to correct problems in collections; and

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.text: The collector's responsibility for maintaining the integrity of the collection process, ensuring the privacy of employees being tested, ensuring the security of the specimen, and avoiding conduct or statements that could be viewed as offensive or inappropriate.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b). Qualification training must provide instruction on the following subjects:

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections for each device you will use.

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: The five mock collections for each device must include one uneventful collection scenario, one insufficient specimen quantity scenario; one scenario in which the employee has something in their mouth that might interfere with the collection; one scenario in which the employee attempts to tamper with the specimen; and one scenario in which the employee refuses to sign the CCF. For each of the five mock collections, the collector must check the expiration date of the device, show it to the employee, and record the date on the CCF used. The collector must ensure, when applying the labels, they do not cover the expiration dates.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in collections under this part by completing five consecutive error-free mock collections for each device you will use.

leaves.heading: § 40.35 What training requirements must a collector meet for oral fluid collection?
leaves.text: Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between you and the qualified collector, who must attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” Except as provided in paragraph (c)(3) of this section, this person must be a qualified oral fluid collector who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by—

leaves.text: Regularly conducting DOT oral fluid drug test collections for a period of at least one year;

leaves.text: As the person monitoring and evaluating the collector's five mock collections pursuant to paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section, you need not be a qualified oral fluid collector to do so if you meet the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities in paragraph (c)(2)(ii) or (iii) until otherwise specified (one year after HHS publishes a Federal Register notification of the first certified oral fluid drug testing laboratory (HHS notification)). Furthermore, the one-year requirement in paragraph (c)(2)(ii) is not applicable until otherwise specified (one year after the HHS notification).

leaves.heading: § 40.36 What information about the DER must employers provide to collectors?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must provide to collectors the name and telephone number of the appropriate DER (and C/TPA, where applicable) to contact about any problems or issues that may arise during the testing process.

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: The Federal Drug Testing Custody and Control Form (CCF) must be used to document every collection required by the DOT drug testing program. You may view this form on the Department's website ( https://www.transportation.gov/odapc ) or the HHS website ( https://www.workplace.samhsa.gov ).

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: You must not use a non-Federal form or an expired CCF to conduct a DOT collection. As a laboratory, C/TPA or other party that provides CCFs to employers, collection sites, or other customers, you must not provide copies of an expired CCF to these participants. You must also affirmatively notify these participants that they must not use an expired CCF.

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: You may include, in the area outside the border of the form, other information needed for billing or other purposes necessary to the collection process.

context.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: The CCF must include the names, addresses, telephone numbers and any other appropriate contact information ( e.g., an email address of the employer and the MRO), including the DER's name and contact information. All of this information must be preprinted, typed, or handwritten. Fax numbers may be included but are not required. The MRO information must include the physician's name and address, as opposed to only a generic clinic, health care organization, company name, or post office box. This information is required, and an employer, collector, service agent or any other party is prohibited from omitting it. In addition, a C/TPA's name, address, telephone and fax numbers, and any other appropriate contact information should be included, but is not required. The employer may use a C/TPA's address in place of its own, but must continue to include its name, telephone and fax numbers, and any other appropriate contact information.

context.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: As an employer you may preprint the box in Step 1-D of the CCF for the DOT agency under whose authority the test will occur.

context.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: As a collector, you may use a CCF with your name, address, telephone number, and fax number preprinted, but under no circumstances may you sign the form before the collection event. If a collection takes place at a clinic, the actual address of the clinic should be used, not a corporate address of the collection company. If the collection takes place onsite at the employer, the employer's address must be noted as the collection site address. If the collection takes place in a “mobile unit” or at an accident site, the collector must enter the actual location address of the collection or as near an approximation as possible. The collector must ensure that the required collector telephone number is the number that the laboratory, MRO, or employer may use to directly contact the individual collector and/or the collector's supervisor during the collection site's business hours. The collector must not provide a number for a call center.

context.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: When using an electronic CCF, you must establish adequate confidentiality and security measures to ensure that confidential employee records are not available to unauthorized persons. This includes protecting the physical security of records, access controls, and computer security measures to safeguard confidential data in electronic form.

context.text: As a participant in the DOT drug testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the CCF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: Under no circumstances may the CCF transmit personal identifying information about an employee (other than a SSN or Employee ID No.) to a laboratory.

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: As an employer, you may use an equivalent foreign-language version of the CCF approved by ODAPC. You may use such a non-English language form only in a situation where both the employee and collector understand and can use the form in that language.

leaves.heading: § 40.40 What form is used to document a DOT collection?
leaves.text: An employer who uses an electronic CCF must ensure that the collection site, the primary and split laboratories, and MRO have compatible systems, and that the employee and any other program participants in the testing process will receive a legible copy of the CCF.

leaves.heading: § 40.41 May employers use the CCF for non-Federal collections or non-Federal forms for DOT collections?
leaves.text: No, as an employer, you are prohibited from using the CCF for non-Federal collections. You are also prohibited from using non-Federal forms for DOT collections. Doing either subjects you to enforcement action under DOT agency regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.41 May employers use the CCF for non-Federal collections or non-Federal forms for DOT collections?
leaves.text: In the rare case where the collector, either by mistake or as the only means to conduct a test under difficult circumstances ( e.g., post-accident or reasonable suspicion test with insufficient time to obtain the CCF), uses a non-Federal form for a DOT collection, the use of a non-Federal form does not present a reason for the laboratory to reject the specimen for testing or for an MRO to cancel the result.

leaves.heading: § 40.41 May employers use the CCF for non-Federal collections or non-Federal forms for DOT collections?
leaves.text: The use of the non-Federal form is a “correctable flaw.” As an MRO, to correct the problem you must follow the procedures of § 40.205(b)(2).

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: A urine collection for a DOT drug test must take place in a collection site meeting the requirements of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating a collection site, you must ensure that it meets the security requirements of § 40.43.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating a collection site, you must have all necessary personnel, materials, equipment, facilities and supervision to provide for the collection, temporary storage, and shipping of urine specimens to a laboratory, and a suitable clean surface for writing.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: Your collection site must include a facility for urination described in either paragraph (e) or paragraph (f) of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: The first, and preferred, type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a single-toilet room, having a full-length privacy door, within which urination can occur.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: No one but the employee may be present in the room during the collection, except for the observer in the event of a directly observed collection.

context.text: The first, and preferred, type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a single-toilet room, having a full-length privacy door, within which urination can occur.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: You must have a source of water for washing hands, that, if practicable, should be external to the closed room where urination occurs. If an external source is not available, you may meet this requirement by securing all sources of water and other substances that could be used for adulteration and substitution ( e.g., water faucets, soap dispensers) and providing moist towelettes outside the closed room.

context.text: The first, and preferred, type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a single-toilet room, having a full-length privacy door, within which urination can occur.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: Such a site must provide substantial visual privacy ( e.g., a toilet stall with a partial-length door) and meet all other applicable requirements of this section.

context.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: If you use a multi-stall restroom, you must either—

context.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: Secure all sources of water and other substances that could be used for adulteration and substitution ( e.g., water faucets, soap dispensers) and place bluing agent in all toilets or secure the toilets to prevent access; or

context.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.
If you use a multi-stall restroom, you must either—

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: Conduct all collections in the facility as monitored collections (see § 40.69 for procedures). This is the only circumstance in which you may conduct a monitored collection.

context.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.
If you use a multi-stall restroom, you must either—

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: No one but the employee may be present in the multistall restroom during the collection, except for the monitor in the event of a monitored collection or the observer in the event of a directly observed collection.

context.text: The second type of facility for urination that a collection site may include is a multistall restroom.

leaves.heading: § 40.42 Where does a urine collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: A collection site may be in a medical facility, a mobile facility ( e.g., a van), a dedicated collection facility, or any other location meeting the requirements of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Collectors and operators of collection sites must take the steps listed in this section to prevent unauthorized access that could compromise the integrity of collections.

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Secure any water sources or otherwise make them unavailable to employees ( e.g., turn off water inlet, tape handles to prevent opening faucets);

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Ensure that the water in the toilet is blue;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Ensure that no soap, disinfectants, cleaning agents, or other possible adulterants are present;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Inspect the site to ensure that no foreign or unauthorized substances are present;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Tape or otherwise secure shut any movable toilet tank top, or put bluing in the tank;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Ensure that undetected access ( e.g., through a door not in your view) is not possible;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Secure areas and items ( e.g., ledges, trash receptacles, paper towel holders, under-sink areas) that appear suitable for concealing contaminants; and

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Recheck items in paragraphs (b)(1) through (7) of this section following each collection to ensure the site's continued integrity.

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: If the collection site uses a facility normally used for other purposes, like a public rest room or hospital examining room, you must, as a collector, also ensure before the collection that:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Access to collection materials and specimens is effectively restricted; and

context.text: If the collection site uses a facility normally used for other purposes, like a public rest room or hospital examining room, you must, as a collector, also ensure before the collection that:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: The facility is secured against access during the procedure to ensure privacy to the employee and prevent distraction of the collector. Limited-access signs must be posted.

context.text: If the collection site uses a facility normally used for other purposes, like a public rest room or hospital examining room, you must, as a collector, also ensure before the collection that:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: To avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting a collection for only one employee at a time. However, during the time one employee is in the period for drinking fluids in a “shy bladder” situation (see § 40.193(b)), you may conduct a collection for another employee.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: To the greatest extent you can, keep an employee's collection container within view of both you and the employee between the time the employee has urinated and the specimen is sealed.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Ensure you are the only person in addition to the employee who handles the specimen before it is poured into the bottles and sealed with tamper-evident seals.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: In the time between when the employee gives you the specimen and when you seal the specimen, remain within the collection site.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.43 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of urine collections?
leaves.text: Maintain personal control over each specimen and CCF throughout the collection process.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.text: If you are operating a collection site, you must implement a policy and procedures to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering any part of the site in which urine specimens are collected or stored.

leaves.text: Only employees being tested, collectors and other collection site workers, DERs, employee and employer representatives authorized by the employer ( e.g., employer policy, collective bargaining agreement), and DOT agency representatives are authorized persons for purposes of this paragraph (e).

leaves.text: Except for the observer in a directly observed collection or the monitor in the case of a monitored collection, you must not permit anyone to enter the urination facility in which employees provide specimens.

leaves.text: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, you must use a shipping container that adequately protects the specimen bottles from shipment damage in the transport of specimens from the collection site to the laboratory.

leaves.heading: § 40.45 What materials are used to send urine specimens to the laboratory?
leaves.text: You are not required to use a shipping container if a laboratory courier hand-delivers the specimens from the collection site to the laboratory.

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: An oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test must take place in a collection site meeting the requirements of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating an oral fluid collection site:

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: You must ensure that it meets the security requirements of § 40.48;

context.text: If you are operating an oral fluid collection site:

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: The site may be a permanent or temporary facility located either at the work site or at a remote site;

context.text: If you are operating an oral fluid collection site:

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: The site may be in a medical facility, a mobile facility ( e.g., a van), a dedicated collection facility, or any other location meeting the requirements of this section; and

context.text: If you are operating an oral fluid collection site:

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: You must have all necessary personnel, materials, equipment, and facilities that include privacy and supervision to provide for the collection, temporary storage, and shipping of specimens to a laboratory, and a suitable clean surface for writing.

context.text: If you are operating an oral fluid collection site:

leaves.heading: § 40.47 Where does an oral fluid collection for a DOT drug test take place?
leaves.text: If a collection site is not accessible and there is an immediate requirement to collect an oral fluid specimen ( e.g., an accident investigation), another site may be used for the collection, if the collection is performed by a collector who has been trained to collect oral fluid specimens in accordance with this part and the manufacturer's procedures for the collection device.

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Collectors and operators of collection sites must take the steps listed in this section to prevent unauthorized access that could compromise the integrity of collections.

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Ensure that access to collection materials and specimens is effectively restricted;

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Ensure that undetected access ( e.g., through a door not in your view) is not possible; and

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Ensure the security of the facility during the collection process to maintain privacy to the employee and prevent distraction of the collector. Limited-access signs must be posted.

context.text: As a collector, you must do the following before each collection to deter tampering with specimens:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: To avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting a collection for only one employee at a time. However, during the time one employee is in the period for drinking fluids in a “dry mouth” situation ( see § 40.72(b)(1)), you may conduct a collection for another employee as long as the employee with “dry mouth” remains supervised.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: To the greatest extent practicable, keep an employee's collection container within view of both you and the employee between the time the employee has provided the oral fluid specimen and the specimen is sealed.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Ensure you are the only person in addition to the employee who handles the specimen before it is sealed with tamper-evident seals.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: In the time between when the employee gives you the specimen and when you seal the specimen, remain within the collection site.

context.text: As a collector, you must take the following additional steps to ensure security during the collection process:

leaves.heading: § 40.48 What steps must operators of collection sites and collectors take to protect the security and integrity of oral fluid collections?
leaves.text: Maintain personal control over each specimen and CCF throughout the collection process.
