leaves.heading: § 40.210 What kinds of drug tests are permitted under the regulations?
leaves.text: Both urine and oral fluid specimens are authorized for collection and testing under this part. An employer can use one or the other, but not both at the beginning of the testing event. For example, if an employee is sent for a test, either a urine or oral fluid specimen can be collected, but not both simultaneously. However, if there is a problem in the collection that necessitates a second collection ( e.g., insufficient quantity of urine, temperature out of range, or insufficient saliva), then a different specimen type could be chosen by the employer ( i.e., through a standing order or a discussion with the collector) or its service agent ( i.e., if there is no standing order and the service agent cannot contact the DER) to complete the collection process for the testing event. Only urine and oral fluid specimens screened and confirmed at HHS-certified laboratories ( see § 40.81) are allowed for drug testing under this part. Point-of-collection (POC) urine, POC oral fluid drug testing, hair testing, or instant tests are not authorized.

leaves.heading: § 40.211 Who conducts DOT alcohol tests?
leaves.text: Screening test technicians (STTs) and breath alcohol technicians (BATs) meeting their respective requirements of this subpart are the only people authorized to conduct DOT alcohol tests.

leaves.heading: § 40.211 Who conducts DOT alcohol tests?
leaves.text: An STT can conduct only alcohol screening tests, but a BAT can conduct alcohol screening and confirmation tests.

leaves.heading: § 40.211 Who conducts DOT alcohol tests?
leaves.text: As a BAT- or STT-qualified immediate supervisor of a particular employee, you may not act as the STT or BAT when that employee is tested, unless no other STT or BAT is available and DOT agency regulations do not prohibit you from doing so.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: To be permitted to act as a BAT or STT in the DOT alcohol testing program, you must meet each of the requirements of this section:

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: You must be knowledgeable about the alcohol testing procedures in this part and the current DOT guidance. Procedures and guidance are available from ODAPC (Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE., Washington, DC 20590, 202-366-3784, or on the ODAPC Web site, http://www.transportation.gov/odapc ). You must keep current on any changes to these materials. You must subscribe to the ODAPC list-serve at ( https://www.transportation.gov/odapc/get-odapc-email-updates ).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Qualification training must be in accordance with the DOT Model BAT or STT Course, as applicable. The DOT Model Courses are available from ODAPC (Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE., Washington DC, 20590, 202-366-3784, or on the ODAPC web site, http://www.dot.gov/ost/dapc ). The training can also be provided using a course of instruction equivalent to the DOT Model Courses. On request, ODAPC will review BAT and STT instruction courses for equivalency.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Qualification training must include training to proficiency in using the alcohol testing procedures of this part and in the operation of the particular alcohol testing device(s) ( i.e., the ASD(s) or EBT(s)) you will be using.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: The training must emphasize that you are responsible for maintaining the integrity of the testing process, ensuring the privacy of employees being tested, and avoiding conduct or statements that could be viewed as offensive or inappropriate.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: The instructor must be an individual who has demonstrated necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities by regularly conducting DOT alcohol tests as an STT or BAT, as applicable, for a period of at least a year, who has conducted STT or BAT training, as applicable, under this part for a year, or who has successfully completed a “train the trainer” course.

context.text: You must receive qualification training meeting the requirements of this paragraph (b).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in alcohol testing under this part by completing seven consecutive error-free mock tests (BATs) or five consecutive error-free tests (STTs).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Another person must monitor and evaluate your performance, in person or by a means that provides real-time observation and interaction between the instructor and trainee, and attest in writing that the mock collections are “error-free.” This person must be an individual who meets the requirements of paragraph (b)(4) of this section.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in alcohol testing under this part by completing seven consecutive error-free mock tests (BATs) or five consecutive error-free tests (STTs).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: These tests must use the alcohol testing devices ( e.g., EBT(s) or ASD(s)) that you will use as a BAT or STT.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in alcohol testing under this part by completing seven consecutive error-free mock tests (BATs) or five consecutive error-free tests (STTs).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: If you are an STT who will be using an ASD that indicates readings by changes, contrasts, or other readings in color, you must demonstrate as part of the mock test that you are able to discern changes, contrasts, or readings correctly.

context.text: Following your completion of qualification training under paragraph (b) of this section, you must demonstrate proficiency in alcohol testing under this part by completing seven consecutive error-free mock tests (BATs) or five consecutive error-free tests (STTs).

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: You must meet the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section before you begin to perform STT or BAT functions.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: No less frequently than every five years from the date on which you satisfactorily complete the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, you must complete refresher training that meets all the requirements of paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: If you make a mistake in the alcohol testing process that causes a test to be cancelled ( i.e., a fatal or uncorrected flaw), you must undergo error correction training. This training must occur within 30 days of the date you are notified of the error that led to the need for retraining.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Error correction training must be provided and your proficiency documented in writing by a person who meets the requirements of paragraph (b)(4) of this section.

context.text: If you make a mistake in the alcohol testing process that causes a test to be cancelled ( i.e., a fatal or uncorrected flaw), you must undergo error correction training. This training must occur within 30 days of the date you are notified of the error that led to the need for retraining.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Error correction training is required to cover only the subject matter area(s) in which the error that caused the test to be cancelled occurred.

context.text: If you make a mistake in the alcohol testing process that causes a test to be cancelled ( i.e., a fatal or uncorrected flaw), you must undergo error correction training. This training must occur within 30 days of the date you are notified of the error that led to the need for retraining.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: As part of the error correction training, you must demonstrate your proficiency in the alcohol testing procedures of this part by completing three consecutive error-free mock tests. The mock tests must include one uneventful scenario and two scenarios related to the area(s) in which your error(s) occurred. The person providing the training must monitor and evaluate your performance and attest in writing that the mock tests were error-free.

context.text: If you make a mistake in the alcohol testing process that causes a test to be cancelled ( i.e., a fatal or uncorrected flaw), you must undergo error correction training. This training must occur within 30 days of the date you are notified of the error that led to the need for retraining.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: You must maintain documentation showing that you currently meet all requirements of this section. You must provide this documentation on request to DOT agency representatives and to employers and C/TPAs who are negotiating to use your services.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Anyone meeting the requirements of this section to be a BAT may act as an STT, provided that the individual has demonstrated initial proficiency in the operation of the ASD that he or she is using, as provided in paragraph (c) of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.213 What training requirements must STTs and BATs meet?
leaves.text: Law enforcement officers who have been certified by state or local governments to conduct breath alcohol testing are deemed to be qualified as BATs. They are not required to also complete the training requirements of this section in order to act as BATs. In order for a test conducted by such an officer to be accepted under DOT alcohol testing requirements, the officer must have been certified by a state or local government to use the EBT or ASD that was used for the test.

leaves.heading: § 40.215 What information about the DER do employers have to provide to BATs and STTs?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must provide to the STTs and BATs the name and telephone number of the appropriate DER (and C/TPA, where applicable) to contact about any problems or issues that may arise during the testing process.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: A DOT alcohol test must take place at an alcohol testing site meeting the requirements of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating an alcohol testing site, you must ensure that it meets the security requirements of § 40.223.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating an alcohol testing site, you must ensure that it provides visual and aural privacy to the employee being tested, sufficient to prevent unauthorized persons from seeing or hearing test results.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: If you are operating an alcohol testing site, you must ensure that it has all needed personnel, materials, equipment, and facilities to provide for the collection and analysis of breath and/or saliva samples, and a suitable clean surface for writing.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: If an alcohol testing site fully meeting all the visual and aural privacy requirements of paragraph (c) is not readily available, this part allows a reasonable suspicion or post-accident test to be conducted at a site that partially meets these requirements. In this case, the site must afford visual and aural privacy to the employee to the greatest extent practicable.

leaves.heading: § 40.221 Where does an alcohol test take place?
leaves.text: An alcohol testing site can be in a medical facility, a mobile facility ( e.g., a van), a dedicated collection facility, or any other location meeting the requirements of this section.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: If you are a BAT, STT, or other person operating an alcohol testing site, you must prevent unauthorized personnel from entering the testing site.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: The only people you are to treat as authorized persons are employees being tested, BATs, STTs, and other alcohol testing site workers, DERs, employee representatives authorized by the employer ( e.g., on the basis of employer policy or labor-management agreement), and DOT agency representatives.

context.text: If you are a BAT, STT, or other person operating an alcohol testing site, you must prevent unauthorized personnel from entering the testing site.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: You must ensure that all persons are under the supervision of a BAT or STT at all times when permitted into the site.

context.text: If you are a BAT, STT, or other person operating an alcohol testing site, you must prevent unauthorized personnel from entering the testing site.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: You may remove any person who obstructs, interferes with, or causes unnecessary delay in the testing process.

context.text: If you are a BAT, STT, or other person operating an alcohol testing site, you must prevent unauthorized personnel from entering the testing site.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: As the BAT or STT, you must not allow any person other than you, the employee, or a DOT agency representative to actually witness the testing process (see §§ 40.241-40.255).

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: If you are operating an alcohol testing site, you must ensure that when an EBT or ASD is not being used for testing, you store it in a secure place.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: If you are operating an alcohol testing site, you must ensure that no one other than BATs or other employees of the site have access to the site when an EBT is unsecured.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: As a BAT or STT, to avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting an alcohol test for only one employee at a time.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: When an EBT screening test on an employee indicates an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, and the same EBT will be used for the confirmation test, you are not allowed to use the EBT for a test on another employee before completing the confirmation test on the first employee.

context.text: As a BAT or STT, to avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting an alcohol test for only one employee at a time.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: As a BAT who will conduct both the screening and the confirmation test, you are to complete the entire screening and confirmation process on one employee before starting the screening process on another employee.

context.text: As a BAT or STT, to avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting an alcohol test for only one employee at a time.

leaves.heading: § 40.223 What steps must be taken to protect the security of alcohol testing sites?
leaves.text: You are not allowed to leave the alcohol testing site while the testing process for a given employee is in progress, except to notify a supervisor or contact a DER for assistance in the case an employee or other person who obstructs, interferes with, or unnecessarily delays the testing process.

context.text: As a BAT or STT, to avoid distraction that could compromise security, you are limited to conducting an alcohol test for only one employee at a time.

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: The DOT Alcohol Testing Form (ATF) must be used for every DOT alcohol test. The ATF must be a three-part carbonless manifold form. The ATF is found in appendix I to this part. You may view this form on the ODAPC web site ( http://www.transportation.gov/odapc ).

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: You may include other information needed for billing purposes, outside the boundaries of the form.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: You may use a ATF directly generated by an EBT which omits the space for affixing a separate printed result to the ATF, provided the EBT prints the result directly on the ATF.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: You may use an ATF that has the employer's name, address, and telephone number preprinted. In addition, a C/TPA's name, address, and telephone number may be included, to assist with negative results.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: You may use an ATF in which all pages are printed on white paper. You may modify the ATF by using colored paper, or have clearly discernable borders or designation statements on Copy 2 and Copy 3. When colors are used, they must be green for Copy 2 and blue for Copy 3.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: As a BAT or STT, you may add, on the “Remarks” line of the ATF, the name of the DOT agency under whose authority the test occurred.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: As a BAT or STT, you may use a ATF that has your name, address, and telephone number preprinted, but under no circumstances can your signature be preprinted.

context.text: As an employer in the DOT alcohol testing program, you are not permitted to modify or revise the ATF except as follows:

leaves.heading: § 40.225 What form is used for an alcohol test?
leaves.text: As an employer, you may use an equivalent foreign-language version of the ATF approved by ODAPC. You may use such a non-English language form only in a situation where both the employee and BAT/STT understand and can use the form in that language.

leaves.heading: § 40.227 May employers use the ATF for non-DOT tests, or non-DOT forms for DOT tests?
leaves.text: No, as an employer, BAT, or STT, you are prohibited from using the ATF for non-DOT alcohol tests. You are also prohibited from using non-DOT forms for DOT alcohol tests. Doing either subjects you to enforcement action under DOT agency regulations.

leaves.heading: § 40.227 May employers use the ATF for non-DOT tests, or non-DOT forms for DOT tests?
leaves.text: If the STT or BAT, either by mistake, or as the only means to conduct a test under difficult circumstances ( e.g., post-accident test with insufficient time to obtain the ATF), uses a non-DOT form for a DOT test, the use of a non-DOT form does not, in and of itself, require the employer or service agent to cancel the test. However, in order for the test to be considered valid, a signed statement must be obtained from the STT or BAT in accordance with § 40.271(b) .

leaves.heading: § 40.229 What devices are used to conduct alcohol screening tests?
leaves.text: ASDs listed on ODAPC's Web page for “Approved Screening Devices to Measure Alcohol in Bodily Fluids” and EBTs listed on ODAPC's Web page for “Approved Evidential Breath Measurement Devices” are the only devices you are allowed to use to conduct alcohol screening tests under this part. You may use an ASD for DOT alcohol tests only if there are instructions for its use in this part. An ASD can be used only for screening tests for alcohol, and must not be used for confirmation tests.

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: EBTs on ODAPC's Web page for “Approved Evidential Breath Measurement Devices” that meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section are the only devices you may use to conduct alcohol confirmation tests under this part.

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Provides a printed triplicate result (or three consecutive identical copies of a result) of each breath test;

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Assigns a unique number to each completed test, which the BAT and employee can read before each test and which is printed on each copy of the result;

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Prints, on each copy of the result, the manufacturer's name for the device, its serial number, and the time of the test;

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Distinguishes alcohol from acetone at the 0.02 alcohol concentration level;

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Tests an air blank; and

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.231 What devices are used to conduct alcohol confirmation tests?
leaves.text: Performs an external calibration check.

context.text: To conduct a confirmation test, you must use an EBT that has the following capabilities:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: As an EBT manufacturer, you must submit, for NHTSA approval, a quality assurance plan (QAP) for your EBT before ODAPC places the EBT on its Web page for “Approved Evidential Breath Measurement Devices.”

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: Your QAP must specify the methods used to perform external calibration checks on the EBT, the tolerances within which the EBT is regarded as being in proper calibration, and the intervals at which these checks must be performed. In designating these intervals, your QAP must take into account factors like frequency of use, environmental conditions ( e.g., temperature, humidity, altitude) and type of operation ( e.g., stationary or mobile).

context.text: As an EBT manufacturer, you must submit, for NHTSA approval, a quality assurance plan (QAP) for your EBT before ODAPC places the EBT on its Web page for “Approved Evidential Breath Measurement Devices.”

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: Your QAP must also specify the inspection, maintenance, and calibration requirements and intervals for the EBT.

context.text: As an EBT manufacturer, you must submit, for NHTSA approval, a quality assurance plan (QAP) for your EBT before ODAPC places the EBT on its Web page for “Approved Evidential Breath Measurement Devices.”

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: As the manufacturer, you must include, with each EBT, instructions for its use and care consistent with the QAP.

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: You must follow the manufacturer's instructions (see paragraph (b) of this section), including performance of external calibration checks at the intervals the instructions specify.

context.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: In conducting external calibration checks, you must use only calibration devices appearing on NHTSA's CPL for “Calibrating Units for Breath Alcohol Tests.”

context.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: If an EBT fails an external check of calibration, you must take the EBT out of service. You may not use the EBT again for DOT alcohol testing until it is repaired and passes an external calibration check.

context.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: You must maintain records of the inspection, maintenance, and calibration of EBTs as provided in § 40.333(a)(3).

context.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.233 What are the requirements for proper use and care of EBTs?
leaves.text: You must ensure that inspection, maintenance, and calibration of the EBT are performed by its manufacturer or a maintenance representative certified either by the manufacturer or by a state health agency or other appropriate state agency.

context.text: As the user of the EBT ( e.g., employer, service agent), you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.235 What are the requirements for proper use and care of ASDs?
leaves.text: As an ASD manufacturer, you must submit, for NHTSA approval, a QAP for your ASD before NHTSA approves it and ODAPC places the device on its Web page for “Approved Screening Devices to Measure Alcohol in Bodily Fluids”. Your QAP must specify the methods used for quality control checks, temperatures at which the ASD must be stored and used, the shelf life of the device, and environmental conditions ( e.g., temperature, altitude, humidity) that may affect the ASD's performance.

leaves.heading: § 40.235 What are the requirements for proper use and care of ASDs?
leaves.text: As a manufacturer, you must include with each ASD instructions for its use and care consistent with the QAP. The instructions must include directions on the proper use of the ASD, and, where applicable the time within which the device must be read, and the manner in which the reading is made.

leaves.heading: § 40.235 What are the requirements for proper use and care of ASDs?
leaves.text: As the user of the ADS ( e.g., employer, STT), you must follow the QAP instructions.

leaves.heading: § 40.235 What are the requirements for proper use and care of ASDs?
leaves.text: You are not permitted to use an ASD that does not pass the specified quality control checks or that has passed its expiration date.

leaves.heading: § 40.235 What are the requirements for proper use and care of ASDs?
leaves.text: As an employer, with respect to breath ASDs, you must also follow the device use and care requirements of § 40.233 .

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: As the BAT or STT you will take the following steps to begin all alcohol screening tests, regardless of the type of testing device you are using:

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: When a specific time for an employee's test has been scheduled, or the collection site is at the employee's worksite, and the employee does not appear at the collection site at the scheduled time, contact the DER to determine the appropriate interval within which the DER has determined the employee is authorized to arrive. If the employee's arrival is delayed beyond that time, you must notify the DER that the employee has not reported for testing. In a situation where a C/TPA has notified an owner/operator or other individual employee to report for testing and the employee does not appear, the C/TPA must notify the employee that he or she has refused to test.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: Ensure that, when the employee enters the alcohol testing site, you begin the alcohol testing process without undue delay. For example, you must not wait because the employee says he or she is not ready or because an authorized employer or employee representative is delayed in arriving.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: If the employee is also going to take a DOT drug test, you must, to the greatest extent practicable, ensure that the alcohol test is completed before the urine collection process begins.

context.text: Ensure that, when the employee enters the alcohol testing site, you begin the alcohol testing process without undue delay. For example, you must not wait because the employee says he or she is not ready or because an authorized employer or employee representative is delayed in arriving.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: If the employee needs medical attention ( e.g., an injured employee in an emergency medical facility who is required to have a post-accident test), do not delay this treatment to conduct a test.

context.text: Ensure that, when the employee enters the alcohol testing site, you begin the alcohol testing process without undue delay. For example, you must not wait because the employee says he or she is not ready or because an authorized employer or employee representative is delayed in arriving.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: Require the employee to provide positive identification. You must see a photo ID issued by the employer (other than in the case of an owner-operator or other self-employer individual) or a Federal, state, or local government ( e.g., a driver's license). You may not accept faxes or photocopies of identification. Positive identification by an employer representative (not a co-worker or another employee being tested) is also acceptable. If the employee cannot produce positive identification, you must contact a DER to verify the identity of the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: If the employee asks, provide your identification to the employee. Your identification must include your name and your employer's name but is not required to include your picture, address, or telephone number.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: Explain the testing procedure to the employee, including showing the employee the instructions on the back of the ATF.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: Complete Step 1 of the ATF.

leaves.heading: § 40.241 What are the first steps in any alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: Direct the employee to complete Step 2 on the ATF and sign the certification. If the employee refuses to sign this certification, you must document this refusal on the “Remarks” line of the ATF and immediately notify the DER. This is a refusal to test.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: As the BAT or STT, you must take the following steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: Select, or allow the employee to select, an individually wrapped or sealed mouthpiece from the testing materials.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: Open the individually wrapped or sealed mouthpiece in view of the employee and insert it into the device in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: Instruct the employee to blow steadily and forcefully into the mouthpiece for at least six seconds or until the device indicates that an adequate amount of breath has been obtained.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: Show the employee the displayed test result.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: If the device is one that prints the test number, testing device name and serial number, time, and result directly onto the ATF, you must check to ensure that the information has been printed correctly onto the ATF.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: If the device is one that prints the test number, testing device name and serial number, time and result, but on a separate printout rather than directly onto the ATF, you must affix the printout of the information to the designated space on the ATF with tamper-evident tape or use a self-adhesive label that is tamper-evident.

leaves.heading: § 40.243 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using an EBT or non-evidential breath ASD?
leaves.text: If the device is one that does not print the test number, testing device name and serial number, time, and result, or it is a device not being used with a printer, you must record this information in Step 3 of the ATF.

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Check the expiration date on the device or on the package containing the device and show it to the employee. You may not use the device after its expiration date.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Open an individually wrapped or sealed package containing the device in the presence of the employee.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Offer the employee the opportunity to use the device. If the employee uses it, you must instruct the employee to insert it into his or her mouth and use it in a manner described by the device's manufacturer.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If the employee chooses not to use the device, or in all cases in which a new test is necessary because the device did not activate (see paragraph (a)(7) of this section), you must insert the device into the employee's mouth and gather saliva in the manner described by the device's manufacturer. You must wear single-use examination or similar gloves while doing so and change them following each test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: When the device is removed from the employee's mouth, you must follow the manufacturer's instructions regarding necessary next steps in ensuring that the device has activated.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you were unable to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (a)(3) through (a)(5) of this section ( e.g., the device breaks, you drop the device on the floor), you must discard the device and conduct a new test using a new device.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: The new device you use must be one that has been under your control or that of the employer before the test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must note on the “Remarks” line of the ATF the reason for the new test. (Note: You may continue using the same ATF with which you began the test.)

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must offer the employee the choice of using the device or having you use it unless the employee, in the opinion of the STT or BAT, was responsible ( e.g., the employee dropped the device) for the new test needing to be conducted.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you are unable to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (a)(3) through (a)(5) of this section on the new test, you must end the collection and put an explanation on the “Remarks” line of the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must then direct the employee to take a new test immediately, using an EBT for the screening test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you are able to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (a)(3)-(a)(5) of this section, but the device does not activate, you must discard the device and conduct a new test, in the same manner as provided in paragraph (a)(6) of this section. In this case, you must place the device into the employee's mouth to collect saliva for the new test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must read the result displayed on the device no sooner than the device's manufacturer instructs. In all cases the result displayed must be read within 15 minutes of the test. You must then show the device and it's reading to the employee and enter the result on the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must never re-use devices, swabs, gloves or other materials used in saliva testing.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must note the fact that you used a saliva ASD in Step 3 of the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the saliva ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Check the expiration date on the detector device and the electronic analyzer or on the package containing the device and the analyzer and show it to the employee. You must not use the device or the analyzer after their expiration date. You must not use an analyzer which is not specifically pre-calibrated for the device being used in the collection.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Remove the device from the package and secure an inflation bag onto the appropriate end of the device, as directed by the manufacturer on the device's instructions.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Break the tube's ampoule in the presence of the employee.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: Offer the employee the opportunity to use the device. If the employee chooses to use ( e.g. hold) the device, instruct the employee to blow forcefully and steadily into the blowing end of device until the inflation bag fills with air (approximately 12 seconds).

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If the employee chooses not to hold the device, you must hold it and provide the use instructions in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: When the employee completes the breath process, take the device from the employee (or if you were holding it, remove it from the employee's mouth), remove the inflation bag, and prepare the device to be read by the analyzer in accordance with the manufacturer's directions.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you were unable to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (b)(4) through (b)(6) of this section ( e.g., the device breaks apart, the employee did not fill the inflation bag), you must discard the device and conduct a new test using a new one.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: The new device you use must be one that has been under your control or that of the employer before the test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must note on the “Remarks” line of the ATF the reason for the new test. (Note: You may continue using the same ATF with which you began the test.)

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must offer the employee the choice of holding the device or having you hold it unless the employee, in the your opinion, was responsible ( e.g., the employee failed to fill the inflation bag) for the new test needing to be conducted.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you are unable to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (b)(4) through (b)(6) of this section on the new test, you must end the collection and put an explanation on the “Remarks” line of the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must then direct the employee to take a new test immediately, using another type of ASD ( e.g., saliva device) or an EBT.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: If you were able to successfully follow the procedures of paragraphs (b)(4) through (b)(6) of this section and after having waited the required amount of time directed by the manufacturer for the detector device to incubate, you must place the device in the analyzer in accordance with the manufacturer's directions. The result must be read from the analyzer no earlier then the required incubation time of the device. In all cases, the result must be read within 15 minutes of the test.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must follow the manufacturer's instructions for determining the result of the test. You must show the analyzer result to the employee and record the result on Step 3 of the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must never re-use detector devices or any gloves used in breath tube testing. The inflation bag must be voided of air following removal from a device. Inflation bags and electronic analyzers may be re-used but only in accordance with the manufacturer's directions.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.245 What is the procedure for an alcohol screening test using a saliva ASD or a breath tube ASD?
leaves.text: You must note the fact that you used a breath tube device in Step 3 of the ATF.

context.text: As the STT or BAT, you must take the following steps when using the breath tube ASD:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of less than 0.02, as the BAT or STT, you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Sign and date Step 3 of the ATF; and

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of less than 0.02, as the BAT or STT, you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Transmit the result to the DER in a confidential manner, as provided in § 40.255 .

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of less than 0.02, as the BAT or STT, you must do the following:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If you are the BAT who will conduct the confirmation test, you must then conduct the test using the procedures beginning at § 40.251 .

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If you are not the BAT who will conduct the confirmation test, direct the employee to take a confirmation test, sign and date Step 3 of the ATF, and give the employee Copy 2 of the ATF.

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Advise the employee not to eat, drink, put anything ( e.g., cigarette, chewing gum) into his or her mouth, or belch;

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Tell the employee the reason for the waiting period required by § 40.251(a) ( i.e., to prevent an accumulation of mouth alcohol from leading to an artificially high reading);

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Explain that following your instructions concerning the waiting period is to the employee's benefit;

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Explain that the confirmation test will be conducted at the end of the waiting period, even if the instructions have not been followed;

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Note on the “Remarks” line of the ATF that the waiting period instructions were provided;

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Instruct the person accompanying the employee to carry a copy of the ATF to the BAT who will perform the confirmation test; and

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: Ensure that you or another BAT, STT, or employer representative observe the employee as he or she is transported to the confirmation testing site. You must direct the employee not to attempt to drive a motor vehicle to the confirmation testing site.

context.text: If the test result is an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or higher, as the BAT or STT, you must direct the employee to take a confirmation test.
If the confirmation test will be performed at a different site from the screening test, you must take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.247 What procedures does the BAT or STT follow after a screening test result?
leaves.text: If the screening test is invalid, you must, as the BAT or STT, tell the employee the test is cancelled and note the problem on the “Remarks” line of the ATF. If practicable, repeat the testing process (see § 40.271).

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: As the BAT for an alcohol confirmation test, you must follow these steps to begin the confirmation test process:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must ensure that the waiting period lasts at least 15 minutes, starting with the completion of the screening test. After the waiting period has elapsed, you should begin the confirmation test as soon as possible, but not more than 30 minutes after the completion of the screening test.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If the confirmation test is taking place at a different location from the screening test (see § 40.247(b)(3)) the time of transit between sites counts toward the waiting period if the STT or BAT who conducted the screening test provided the waiting period instructions.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

You must ensure that the waiting period lasts at least 15 minutes, starting with the completion of the screening test. After the waiting period has elapsed, you should begin the confirmation test as soon as possible, but not more than 30 minutes after the completion of the screening test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If you cannot verify, through review of the ATF, that waiting period instructions were provided, then you must carry out the waiting period requirement.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

You must ensure that the waiting period lasts at least 15 minutes, starting with the completion of the screening test. After the waiting period has elapsed, you should begin the confirmation test as soon as possible, but not more than 30 minutes after the completion of the screening test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You or another BAT or STT, or an employer representative, must observe the employee during the waiting period.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

You must ensure that the waiting period lasts at least 15 minutes, starting with the completion of the screening test. After the waiting period has elapsed, you should begin the confirmation test as soon as possible, but not more than 30 minutes after the completion of the screening test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Concerning the waiting period, you must tell the employee:

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Not to eat, drink, put anything ( e.g., cigarette, chewing gum) into his or her mouth, or belch;

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:
Concerning the waiting period, you must tell the employee:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: The reason for the waiting period ( i.e., to prevent an accumulation of mouth alcohol from leading to an artificially high reading);

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:
Concerning the waiting period, you must tell the employee:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: That following your instructions concerning the waiting period is to the employee's benefit; and

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:
Concerning the waiting period, you must tell the employee:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: That the confirmation test will be conducted at the end of the waiting period, even if the instructions have not been followed.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:
Concerning the waiting period, you must tell the employee:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If you become aware that the employee has not followed the instructions, you must note this on the “Remarks” line of the ATF.

context.text: You must carry out a requirement for a waiting period before the confirmation test, by taking the following steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If you did not conduct the screening test for the employee, you must require positive identification of the employee, explain the confirmation procedures, and use a new ATF. You must note on the “Remarks” line of the ATF that a different BAT or STT conducted the screening test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Complete Step 1 of the ATF.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Direct the employee to complete Step 2 on the ATF and sign the certification. If the employee refuses to sign this certification, you must document this refusal on the “Remarks” line of the ATF and immediately notify the DER. This is a refusal to test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Even if more than 30 minutes have passed since the screening test result was obtained, you must begin the confirmation test procedures in § 40.253, not another screening test.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must note on the “Remarks” line of the ATF the time that elapsed between the two events, and if the confirmation test could not begin within 30 minutes of the screening test, the reason why.

leaves.heading: § 40.251 What are the first steps in an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: Beginning the confirmation test procedures after the 30 minutes have elapsed does not invalidate the screening or confirmation tests, but it may constitute a regulatory violation subject to DOT agency sanction.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: As the BAT conducting an alcohol confirmation test, you must follow these steps in order to complete the confirmation test process:

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: In the presence of the employee, you must conduct an air blank on the EBT you are using before beginning the confirmation test and show the reading to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If the reading is 0.00, the test may proceed. If the reading is greater than 0.00, you must conduct another air blank.

context.text: In the presence of the employee, you must conduct an air blank on the EBT you are using before beginning the confirmation test and show the reading to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If the reading on the second air blank is 0.00, the test may proceed. If the reading is greater than 0.00, you must take the EBT out of service.

context.text: In the presence of the employee, you must conduct an air blank on the EBT you are using before beginning the confirmation test and show the reading to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If you take an EBT out of service for this reason, no one may use it for testing until the EBT is found to be within tolerance limits on an external check of calibration.

context.text: In the presence of the employee, you must conduct an air blank on the EBT you are using before beginning the confirmation test and show the reading to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must proceed with the test of the employee using another EBT, if one is available.

context.text: In the presence of the employee, you must conduct an air blank on the EBT you are using before beginning the confirmation test and show the reading to the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must open a new individually wrapped or sealed mouthpiece in view of the employee and insert it into the device in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must ensure that you and the employee read the unique test number displayed on the EBT.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must instruct the employee to blow steadily and forcefully into the mouthpiece for at least six seconds or until the device indicates that an adequate amount of breath has been obtained.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must show the employee the result displayed on the EBT.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: You must show the employee the result and unique test number that the EBT prints out either directly onto the ATF or onto a separate printout.

leaves.heading: § 40.253 What are the procedures for conducting an alcohol confirmation test?
leaves.text: If the EBT provides a separate printout of the result, you must attach the printout to the designated space on the ATF with tamper-evident tape, or use a self-adhesive label that is tamper-evident.

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: Sign and date Step 3 of the ATF.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: If the alcohol confirmation test result is lower than 0.02, nothing further is required of the employee. As the BAT, you must sign and date Step 3 of the ATF.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: If the alcohol confirmation test result is 0.02 or higher, direct the employee to sign and date Step 4 of the ATF. If the employee does not do so, you must note this on the “Remarks” line of the ATF. However, this is not considered a refusal to test.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: If the test is invalid, tell the employee the test is cancelled and note the problem on the “Remarks” line of the ATF. If practicable, conduct a re-test. (see § 40.271).

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: Immediately transmit the result directly to the DER in a confidential manner.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: You may transmit the results using Copy 1 of the ATF, in person, by telephone, or by electronic means. In any case, you must immediately notify the DER of any result of 0.02 or greater by any means ( e.g., telephone or secure fax machine) that ensures the result is immediately received by the DER. You must not transmit these results through C/TPAs or other service agents.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:
Immediately transmit the result directly to the DER in a confidential manner.

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: If you do not make the initial transmission in writing, you must follow up the initial transmission with Copy 1 of the ATF.

context.text: After the EBT has printed the result of an alcohol confirmation test, you must, as the BAT, take the following additional steps:
Immediately transmit the result directly to the DER in a confidential manner.

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: As an employer, you must take the following steps with respect to the receipt and storage of alcohol test result information:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: If you receive any test results that are not in writing ( e.g., by telephone or electronic means), you must establish a mechanism to establish the identity of the BAT sending you the results.

context.text: As an employer, you must take the following steps with respect to the receipt and storage of alcohol test result information:

leaves.heading: § 40.255 What happens next after the alcohol confirmation test result?
leaves.text: You must store all test result information in a way that protects confidentiality.

context.text: As an employer, you must take the following steps with respect to the receipt and storage of alcohol test result information:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to appear for any test (except a pre-employment test) within a reasonable time, as determined by the employer, consistent with applicable DOT agency regulations, after being directed to do so by the employer. This includes the failure of an employee (including an owner-operator) to appear for a test when called by a C/TPA (see § 40.241(a));

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to remain at the testing site until the testing process is complete. Provided that an employee who leaves the collection site before the testing process commences ( see § 40.243(a)) for a pre-employment test is not deemed to have refused to test. The BAT or STT is not required to inform an employee that the failure to remain at the collection site is a refusal. If an employee leaves prior to the completion of the testing process, per § 40.355(i) the employer must decide whether the employee's actions constitute a refusal;

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to provide an adequate amount of saliva or breath for any alcohol test required by this part or DOT agency regulations; Provided that an employee who does not provide an adequate amount of breath or saliva because he or she has left the testing site before the testing process commences ( see § 40.243(a)) for a pre-employment test is not deemed to have refused to test. The BAT or STT is not required to inform an employee that the failure to remain at the collection site is a refusal. If an employee leaves prior to the completion of the testing process, per § 40.355(i) the employer must decide whether the employee's actions constitute a refusal;

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to provide a sufficient breath specimen, and the physician has determined, through a required medical evaluation, that there was no adequate medical explanation for the failure (see § 40.265(c));

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to undergo a medical examination or evaluation, as directed by the employer as part of the insufficient breath procedures outlined at § 40.265(c);

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to sign the certification at Step 2 of the ATF (see §§ 40.241(g) and 40.251(d)); or

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: Fail to cooperate with any part of the testing process.

context.text: As an employee, you are considered to have refused to take an alcohol test if you:

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: As an employee, if you refuse to take an alcohol test, you incur the same consequences specified under DOT agency regulations for a violation of those DOT agency regulations. The consequences specified under DOT agency regulations for a refusal cannot be overturned or set aside by an arbitration, grievance, State court or other non-Federal forum that adjudicates the personnel decisions the employer has taken against the employee.

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: As a BAT or an STT, or as the physician evaluating a “shy lung” situation, when an employee refuses to test as provided in paragraph (a) of this section, you must terminate the portion of the testing process in which you are involved, document the refusal on the ATF (or in a separate document which you cause to be attached to the form), immediately notify the DER by any means ( e.g., telephone or secure fax machine) that ensures the refusal notification is immediately received. You must make this notification directly to the DER (not using a C/TPA as an intermediary).

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: As the BAT or STT, you must note the actions that may constitute a refusal in the “Remarks” line (Step 3), and sign and date the ATF. The BAT or STT does not make the final decision about whether the employee's conduct constitutes a refusal to test; the employer has the sole responsibility to decide whether a refusal occurred, as stated in § 40.355(i), the employer has a non-delegable duty to make the decision about whether the employee has refused to test.

leaves.heading: § 40.261 What is a refusal to take an alcohol test, and what are the consequences?
leaves.text: As an employee, when you refuse to take a non-DOT test or to sign a non-DOT form, you have not refused to take a DOT test. There are no consequences under DOT agency regulations for such a refusal.

leaves.heading: § 40.263 What happens when an employee is unable to provide a sufficient amount of saliva for an alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: As the STT, you must take the following steps if an employee is unable to provide sufficient saliva to complete a test on a saliva screening device ( e.g., the employee does not provide sufficient saliva to activate the device).

leaves.heading: § 40.263 What happens when an employee is unable to provide a sufficient amount of saliva for an alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: You must conduct a new screening test using a new screening device.

context.text: As the STT, you must take the following steps if an employee is unable to provide sufficient saliva to complete a test on a saliva screening device ( e.g., the employee does not provide sufficient saliva to activate the device).

leaves.heading: § 40.263 What happens when an employee is unable to provide a sufficient amount of saliva for an alcohol screening test?
leaves.text: If the employee refuses to make the attempt to complete the new test, you must discontinue testing, note the fact on the “Remarks” line of the ATF, and immediately notify the DER. This is a refusal to test.

context.text: As the STT, you must take the following steps if an employee is unable to provide sufficient saliva to complete a test on a saliva screening device ( e.g., the employee does not provide sufficient saliva to activate the device).

leaves.heading: § 40.263 What happens when an employee is unable to provide a sufficient amount of saliva for an alcohol screening test?
